summary: Top-up on the production build (e30b837, sw kos-redraw-1). All twelve earlier findings still hold and most got worse with the Achievements/art/shop release: boot now loads 346 synchronous scripts (16.9 MB JS, 9.95 MB of it curriculum data) and spends long seconds compiling content before main.js; derived reads are still un-memoised, and the new badge engine re-measures all 254 badges on every Seat/Wall render and tab switch, so first renders of the Governor, shop and Wall cost seconds on the dense account and an owner tick produces ~0.6-0.9 s long tasks. Every boot also runs the exam cap pass over all 5,442 cards with linear leaf scans (0.7-1 s, moving nothing) and readiness about 15 times. There is still no view lifecycle: KOS.rerender drops focus to body, detached pages leak through lazily removed listeners, and a wrong staleness check now lets the Wall's async callback pop a set dialog over whatever page you navigated to; the redraw stopgap's hand-kept TASK_VIEWS list leaves the two new draft pages (Edit your seat, the Wall's Showcase) unprotected. Maintainability: hub.js and aitools.js stay ~3.8-3.9k lines and governor-ui.js has grown to 1,730; the four study spaces still copy the lesson machinery; dead CSS grew (16 governor classes left by the Stage rebuild). Docs drift is the most user-facing structural problem: README/PROGRESS/HANDOFF name releases a week or more old, AGENTS.md's gate command skips smoke108 and smoke113, in-app Help covers none of the last six features, and CLAUDE.md is a 186 KB file whose 271-line baseline is a release diary with stale entries.

findings.title: Boot loads ~16.6 MB of JavaScript in 340 synchronous script tags, most of it curriculum content no first view needs
findings.detail: index.html lists 340 <script src> tags; only KaTeX, supabase.js and env.local.js are deferred. Summed on disk: 16.64 MB JS (js/data/content 8.28 MB in 126 files, js/modules 3.33 MB, js/core 2.50 MB, js/data 1.67 MB, js/labs 0.60 MB) plus 1.21 MB CSS in 24 sheets. Every topic's notes for every subject (CS, Maths, IT, Code units 1-12, tracks, Japanese, Mind, Creatives), the 567 KB past-paper index, and the 383 KB Rider project scaffolds (code-projects-files.js, needed only when exporting a Rider zip) are parsed and executed before Home renders. In the harness a cold reload of the EMPTY account took 15.0 s to domInteractive with 61 long tasks totalling 15.4 s (max 2.75 s); the CPU profile shows 11 s of (program) (parse/compile) and the top self-time scripts are content files executing their builders (cs-p2-46b.js 746 ms, code.js lesson() 316 ms, cs-p2-411.js 545 ms, cs-p2-410a.js 497 ms, maths-stats-s4 325 ms...). The machine was shared with other audit slots so absolute times are inflated, but the shape is unambiguous: the content payload dominates boot, and on an iPad/iPhone (slower JS, tighter memory, Safari evicting a backgrounded Home Screen app) every cold launch pays it. Heap after boot on the empty account: 68 MB.
findings.evidence: arch20/boot.mjs runs on slot 20 (6 Nov): {jsN:346, jsMB:16.9, domInteractive:53357, longTasks:78, longMs:51726} and {domInteractive:70719, longTasks:87} on Home; python count of index.html <script src> = 346; arch20/trace-boot-dense.txt (script evaluation, achcatalogue.js 943 ms) | earlier: audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/arch/prof-boot-empty.txt; index.html lines 48-55 (only defer tags) and the 340-script list; sizes via stat: exam-index.js 566,954 B, code-projects-files.js 382,808 B, it-f204.js 299,469 B, hub.js 232,148 B, aitools.js 208,176 B; Performance API: domInteractive 14,993 ms, longtasks 61 / 15,441 ms; dense account warm reload (SW controlling, V8 code cache): data-shell=ready at 21,064 ms, 35 long tasks totalling 19,166 ms, heap 58 MB (machine shared with other audit slots, load avg ~5)
findings.fix: Keep the script-tag architecture but split content into lazily loaded bundles: KOS.content.get(key) already funnels every read, so make content files register a loader per subject/unit (a tiny manifest listing keys -> file) and inject the script on first open of a topic, a desk or search (search can use a prebuilt title/keyword index). Load exam-index.js only on #/exams, code-projects-files.js only on export, ja/mind/creatives content only when their desk opens. Target: boot payload under ~4 MB. Also add performance.mark('kos-boot-start'/'kos-interactive') in main.js so the cost is tracked by a smoke test budget.
findings.rootCause: Classic script-tag design (chosen so file:// works) with no lazy-loading layer; every new study space appended its whole content to index.html.
findings.devices: all; worst on iPhone 17 and iPad (cold launch of the Home Screen app)
findings.recheck: changed: now 346 scripts (4 defer/async), 16.9 MB JS of which js/data 9.95 MB, 26 stylesheets 1.31 MB (was 340 / 16.6 MB / 1.2 MB). Dense boot on slot 20 at machine load 6-10: domInteractive 53-127 s, 78-106 long tasks totalling 52-125 s; evaluating scripts before main.js took ~18 s, and the first KOS.show after main.js 13.7 s when the restored route was the Wall. Absolute times are inflated by the shared machine, the shape holds.

findings.title: Cold-path cost after boot: the first render of each heavy view takes 0.5-2.8 s on the dense account (Exams, Code map, Due, Pacing, Calendar), then 20-200 ms
findings.detail: Rendering each view three times in a row (via a cheap view in between) on the seeded account gave: exams 2750/589/179 ms, code map 1622/504/355, due 1623/263/22, pacing 1405/51/120, calendar 1015/168/189, japanese 825/59/311, routines 705/11/16, mind 670/171/126, home 205/175/63 (first ever Home after boot was 2.0-3.3 s). Steady state is acceptable; the first visit after a cold launch is not, and on an iPad/iPhone Home Screen app every relaunch after Safari evicts it is a cold launch. Two causes: (1) V8 lazily compiles functions from the 16.6 MB of eagerly loaded script on first use, and (2) the derived reads have no per-render snapshot, so first calls are expensive and repeated: KOS.exams.readiness over 17 assessments measured 3,247 ms then 696/78/55 ms on later runs; KOS.code.unitState (js/core/code.js:888) rescans every lesson and calls stats() (code.js:856) per call, and the Code map (js/modules/code.js:417-490) calls it per unit, per track need (needMet) and per track section (trackState); evidence() re-splits shipped notes with KOS.content.splitPages on every call (code.js:168, 66 ms/call measured). The Calendar month calls dayItems -> derivedOn (37 ms/call warm, calendar.js:563) for each of 35-42 cells, re-reading every Money rule, goal and exam start-by per cell.
findings.evidence: arch20/views.js -> arch20/views-out.txt; eval topic1 6735 ms / topic2 3884 ms | earlier: eval timings above (slot 18, seeded); audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/arch/prof-boot-dense.txt (readiness js/core/exams.js:635 1314 ms self in the boot profile, exams.js:945 predictPass 893 ms), arch/prof-code.txt, arch/prof-calendar.txt; js/core/code.js:166-190, 856-895; js/modules/code.js:417-490; js/modules/calendar.js:546-570, 1762-1800; js/core/exams.js:635-720, 943-960
findings.fix: Add a cheap per-tick memo: a KOS.store revision counter bumped by save(), and memoise the heavy pure reads (exams.readiness/leaves, code stats/unitState/pageCount, calendar derivedOn for a month range, srs.allCards) on (args, revision, day). Shipped content is immutable at runtime (invariant 86), so pageCount/listingsOf can be cached forever. For the calendar, compute derived items for the visible range once and bucket by date. Pair with lazy content loading (boot finding) to cut compile cost.
findings.rootCause: Pure derive-on-read design (a good contract) without any memoisation layer, so composite pages multiply the cost; plus eager loading of all code.
findings.devices: all; most felt on iPhone 17 and iPad cold launches
findings.recheck: holds: first/warm render on slot 20 (load 7-10, so ~2-3x inflated): home 6560/4640 ms, calendar 10362/3683, exams 5393/4926, code 6452/2738, pacing 5929/2574, due 2302/857, a CS topic page 6735 then 3884; new heavy views: governor 3090-6101, governor/shop 7341/3436, governor/edit 7167/829, the Wall 1.9-7.9 s until its badges draw.

findings.title: The four study spaces each re-implement the same lesson machinery (paged reader with dwell, evidence, syncChecks, award, planDay), and the copies have already drifted
findings.detail: Code, Japanese, Mind and Creatives each have their own core model (js/core/code.js 942 lines, ja.js 409, mind.js 633, creatives.js 483), topic module (codetopic.js 718, jatopic.js 387, mindtopic.js 442, crtopic.js 266), desk module and UI helper (codeui/jaui/mindui), 9,644 lines in all. Every core defines its own evidence(), syncChecks(), award(), planDay() and normalise(); every topic module carries its own copy of the paged notes reader with DWELL = 2500 / LEAVE = 1500, a page select, dots, markRead and paint (codetopic.js:26-27/354-397, jatopic.js:22/215-244, mindtopic.js:19/271-302, crtopic.js:16/163). A diff of the Japanese and Mind readers (48 lines each) shows 42 changed lines for the same behaviour, with drift a user can see: Japanese labels the pager 'Note pages' and hides it for one-page lessons, Mind labels it 'Lesson pages' and always shows it; Mind's markRead skips a 'Your notes' page, Japanese's has no such guard. The read-dwell rule is invariant 107's, so four copies mean four places to keep in step, and the next study space (roadmap) will add a fifth.
findings.evidence: grep var DWELL js/modules/*topic.js (6 Nov); grep -l function syncChecks|award|planDay js/core | earlier: grep 'var DWELL' in js/modules/{codetopic,jatopic,mindtopic,crtopic}.js; diff of jatopic.js:213-260 vs mindtopic.js:269-316 (42 differing lines); grep 'function syncChecks|function award|function planDay|function evidence' finds one per space in js/core/{code,ja,mind,creatives}.js
findings.fix: Extract a shared KOS.lessonReader({pages, peekRead, markPage, onChanged, label}) into js/core/ (the pager, dots, dwell/leave timing, 'Your notes' guard, Next/Prev) and have the four topic modules mount it; then a small KOS.studySpace helper for the checks-sync pattern (evidence -> want[] -> store.setCheck diff) that each core calls with its own evidence(). Do it before the next study space rather than as a rewrite: start with the reader, which has the visible drift.
findings.rootCause: Each study space was built in its own release branch by copying the previous one (comments say 'the pager as Code's and Japanese's'), with no shared component extracted afterwards.
findings.recheck: holds: var DWELL in codetopic/jatopic/mindtopic/crtopic (codetopic still differs: no LEAVE); syncChecks, award and planDay each defined in code.js, creatives.js, ja.js, mind.js; jatopic.js:213-260 vs mindtopic.js:269-316 still 42 differing lines.

findings.title: Detached pages leak: global listeners are removed only when their event next fires, so every visited topic/Files/lesson page stays in memory
findings.detail: 15 places add a window/document listener on each render and remove it lazily inside the handler ('if (!node.isConnected) { removeEventListener(...); return; }'): hub.js:2719 and 3169 (kos-ink on every topic page), files.js:283 (paste) and 292 (kos-files-index), attachments.js:736 (paste), inkui.js:1422 (keydown), inktab.js:518, codetopic.js:214/228, jatopic.js:321/334, mindtopic.js:380/395, crtopic.js:246, inksync.js:339. Rare events (kos-ink fires only when ink is written; paste only on a paste) never come, so each closure keeps its whole detached page alive. Measured with forced GC (CDP HeapProfiler.collectGarbage + Memory.getDOMCounters) on the seeded account: on Files, 9,003 DOM nodes / 886 listeners; after opening 30 CS topic pages and returning to Files, 24,954 nodes / 2,369 listeners (about 16,000 detached nodes retained); dispatching one kos-ink event dropped it to 11,027 / 1,096. Three rounds over 23 views grew nodes from 1,786 to 14,110 and listeners from 157 to 1,795. Opening Files 5 times adds 5 document paste listeners. On an iPad Home Screen app kept open for days this is unbounded growth until Safari kills the page (which then pays the full cold boot).
findings.evidence: arch20/mem2.txt and arch20/mem.txt (this build); grep -rEn isConnected[^;]*removeEventListener js | wc -l = 15 | earlier: audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/arch/mem.txt, arch/mem2.txt; eval: 5 paste listeners after 5 Files visits; grep 'isConnected[^;]*removeEventListener' = 15 sites listed
findings.fix: Give KOS.show a teardown hook: views register cleanups via a KOS.ui.onLeave(fn) (or an AbortController per render, passing {signal} to addEventListener) that KOS.show calls before clearing #main; replace the 15 lazy removals with it. Add a smoke check that navigating 20 views leaves the listener count flat (jsdom can count via a wrapped addEventListener).
findings.rootCause: No view lifecycle: KOS.show replaces #main with innerHTML='' and has no unmount step, so each module invented a lazy self-removal.
findings.devices: iPad (long-lived Home Screen app) and iPhone most; all
findings.recheck: holds: still 15 isConnected-lazy removeEventListener sites (inkui, inksync, codetopic, mindtopic, jatopic, files, attachments, hub, inktab, crtopic); on this build 30 CS topic pages left 23,414 nodes / 2,237 listeners on the Files page vs 7,413 / 749 before, released only when a kos-ink event fired (9,487).

findings.title: hub.js is a 3,899-line grab bag: Home (~900 lines), the subject page, a 953-line KOS.views.ref topic function, Backup & Restore, the header search listbox and rail counters
findings.detail: js/modules/hub.js (232 KB) holds the rail counters (KOS.refreshRailCounters :340), the spine toggle (:383), Home's next action/daily goal/Focus ladder (:713-894), KOS.views.home (:1041-1941), KOS.views.subject (:1942-2348), KOS.views.ref (:2349-3301, one 953-line function containing the tab row, ink count, Working pane, pager, inspector wiring), KOS.views.data (Backup, :3302), the topbar search listbox (:3552) and 'the ONE dismissal path' (:3670), plus KOS.hub's shared study statistics. Every study space plugs into KOS.views.ref through flags on cx (e.g. cx.assistStrip=false for Mind), so the topic page is the most coupled function in the app and the one every study-space release edits. Similar giants: js/core/aitools.js 3,811 lines (every Assistant tool for every domain in one file), assistant.js 2,719, focus.js 2,598. The window's KOS namespace has 209 top-level members and about 430 'KOS.x && ...' existence guards in core/modules, which hide load-order mistakes instead of failing.

findings.fix: Necessary (low risk, mechanical): move KOS.views.home and its helpers to js/modules/home.js, Backup & Restore to js/modules/backup.js, the search listbox to js/core/searchui.js; split KOS.views.ref into a topic shell plus per-tab renderers registered by subject (KOS.topicTabs.register), which is also where the study spaces' cx flags belong. Split aitools.js by domain (each owner registers its tools, as goals do). High value: replace silent 'KOS.x &&' guards for hard dependencies with a boot-time assertion of required modules so a load-order slip fails loudly in smoke.
findings.rootCause: Home and the topic page grew in place across Categories 1-7 and every study-space release; the file was never split after the UI rebuild.

findings.title: KOS.rerender() drops keyboard focus to <body> on every redraw, including background ones (cloud pull, habit auto-tick)
findings.detail: Invariant 65 says a redraw changes no focus. KOS.rerender (js/core/ui.js:344-357) re-runs KOS.show(..., {_nav:true}), which empties #main (ui.js, main.innerHTML = '') and rebuilds it; it restores main.scrollTop but not the focused control. Measured on the seeded account: focusing a control and calling KOS.rerender() left document.activeElement = BODY on Home (was home.review-line), Calendar (cal.mode), Routines (ui.tab), Reminders (rem.side-item) and Money (ui.tab). Background callers make this hit keyboard and VoiceOver users without any action of theirs: cloudsync.js:731 rerenderCurrent after a pull, routines.js:699 after autoSync ticks a habit, plus 142 KOS.rerender() call sites in total (most after the user's own action, where the control they used vanishes). A redraw also costs a full view build (225 ms Home, 326 ms Calendar warm).
findings.evidence: eval on slot 20 (6 Nov): {home:{before:"Revise for: AQA 7517 Paper 2",after:"BODY"}, calendar:{before:"Show",after:"BODY"}, money, achievements, governor, routines all BODY}; js/core/ui.js:355-372 | earlier: eval on slot 18: {home:{ms:225,focusedBefore:'home.review-line',after:'BODY'}, calendar:{ms:326,after:'BODY'}, routines, reminders, money all BODY}; js/core/ui.js:344-357; js/core/cloudsync.js:723-731; js/core/routines.js:699
findings.fix: In KOS.rerender, before the redraw record the focused element's identity inside #main (closest [data-ui] plus data-key/data-id/aria-label and its index among matches) and after it focus the equivalent node with {preventScroll:true}, falling back to #main without announcing; skip background redraws while focus is inside #main and the user is typing (or defer them until blur).
findings.rootCause: Redraw is implemented as navigation (rebuild #main) with only scroll restoration.
findings.devices: Mac (keyboard), iPad with keyboard, VoiceOver on all
findings.recheck: holds on kos-redraw-1: the stopgap keeps the scroller position but not focus. Focus a control, KOS.rerender(): home, calendar, money, achievements (Showcase tab button), governor (Avatar) and routines all leave document.activeElement = BODY.

findings.title: Edit your seat loses its unsaved draft (and its tab) on any background redraw: governor is not a held view
findings.detail: #/governor/edit keeps its draft (showcase, background, title, sigil) in a closure inside the view function (js/modules/governor-ui.js:660-686). The kos-redraw-1 stopgap holds background redraws only for TASK_VIEWS (js/core/ui.js:357-358), which does not list governor (nor achievements, money, goals, routines). So a soft background redraw (routines autoSync after a session or on the review ticker, js/core/routines.js:699; the Daily Review closing, js/modules/dayreview.js:92/103/661/709; the Google read-only copy loading, js/core/ext.js:364; own art loading at boot, js/main.js:307) remounts the page at once, and a cloud pull (hard) does so 45 s after the last touch. Repro on slot 20: open Edit your seat, Background tab, pick another background (Save lights up, data-state=lit), call KOS.rerender({background:'soft'}): the tab is back on Showcase, the picked background is gone and Save is no longer lit; nothing was saved. The page has a Discard/Save pair, so the user believes the draft is held until they press one. Top-up 2: the Wall's Showcase tab has the same problem: its picker draft (with its own Save button, js/modules/achievements.js:412-413) is lost on a soft background redraw because achievements is not in TASK_VIEWS either: picked 1 badge (count 1 of 6) -> KOS.rerender({background:soft}) -> 0 of 6, nothing stored.
findings.evidence: eval on slot 20 (seeded): before {tabSel:'Background', mid pressed '1000…', lit:'lit'} → after soft rerender {afterTab:'Showcase', lit2:null}; shots/architecture-perf/gov-edit-mac.png; js/core/ui.js:357-372 (TASK_VIEWS, holdBackground); js/modules/governor-ui.js:660-686; eval slot 20 (6 Nov) Wall showcase {mid:1,cnt:"1 of 6",after:0,cntAfter:"0 of 6",stored:0}
findings.fix: Short term: add governor (the edit arg) and any page with an in-page draft to the held list, or let a view declare itself held (e.g. KOS.views.x.holdsDraft = arg => …) so the list is not a central guess. Proper fix: the view lifecycle in the backlog (a view can veto or persist its draft before a redraw); the Edit seat draft could also live in state.ui like other per-device drafts.
findings.rootCause: The redraw stopgap's hold list is a hand-maintained set of view ids in ui.js; any page added later with transient in-page state is unprotected by default.

findings.title: Badge measuring runs synchronously on the main thread: the Governor's Seat measures all 254 badges twice per render, and every topic tick re-measures 44 study badges
findings.detail: KOS.achievements.list() builds a fresh context (makeCtx, js/core/achievements.js:239) and runs every badge's measure (measureOne, :296) each time it is called; nothing is memoised across calls or renders. The Governor's Seat status page calls it twice per render (js/modules/governor-ui.js:358 the arc of medals and :527 the area cards) and Edit your seat once more (:732); the Wall calls it on each tab (js/modules/achievements.js:126, 613, 747). Many measures are themselves the expensive derived reads the earlier audit found un-memoised — KOS.exams.readiness for every upcoming exam (achcatalogue.js:251-256, the 'Ready' badge), Code/Creatives/Mind evidence over every lesson, topic bands over every leaf for the ~30 unit badges (reg.unit, achcatalogue.js ~246). Owner events re-measure by domain (touch, 400 ms debounce), and the 'study' domain holds 44 badges, so every store.setCheck/setStatus (js/core/store.js:452/466 → onProgress) costs one main-thread long task some 400 ms after the tick. Measured on the dense account (machine shared, load 5-9, so absolute figures are inflated): a single onProgress('cs') produced one 541 ms long task; evaluate(['study']) took 1.3-13.5 s across runs; KOS.achievements.list() 2.4-3.9 s cold, 138 ms warm; KOS.show('governor') 0.7-22 s (3.1 s typical first render), with measureOne, reg.unit, readiness, code/creatives/mind evidence, code.stats and srs.dueCards at the top of its CPU profile. Top-up 2 (load 7-10): KOS.achievements.touch([study]) produced long tasks of 920 and 631 ms; a reload that restores onto #/achievements made its first KOS.show take 13.7 s in the boot wrapper; the Wall shows Reading your records for 1.9-7.9 s on first open and re-measures on every tab switch and every rerender (4.4 s). A no-op full sweep writes nothing (0 store.save calls), which is correct. Measure exceptions are swallowed to null with no console line (achievements.js:307), so a schema change in an owner would silently stop a badge.
findings.evidence: arch20/prof-governor.txt (CPU profile of KOS.show('governor')); eval on slot 20: {listCallsPerGovernorRender:2, list first 3929 ms / second 138 ms, evalStudy 13555 then 3112 then 1324 ms}, longtask observer after KOS.achievements.onProgress('cs') = [541]; js/core/achievements.js:239-262, 296-341, 446-466; js/modules/governor-ui.js:358, 527, 732; arch20/bootsteps.mjs [show 13708 ms on the Wall]; arch20/views-out.txt; eval longtasks after touch [920,631]; savesPerNoopSweep 0
findings.fix: Keep the last evaluate's per-badge values (in memory, keyed by a store revision or the ledgerKey already computed at achievements.js:134) and let list() read them instead of re-measuring; measure only when the owning domain's revision moved. Run the domain re-measure in idle slices (requestIdleCallback, a few badges per slice) so a tick never blocks input. The memo layer for readiness/code evidence recommended in the backlog would cut the rest.
findings.rootCause: list() and evaluate() both measure from scratch with a per-call context; measures reuse un-memoised derived reads; all of it runs synchronously.

findings.title: Opening a Wall set by link and leaving before the badges are measured pops the set dialog over whatever page you are on
findings.detail: KOS.views.achievements draws the Wall in the async KOS.achievements.list() callback (js/modules/achievements.js:126-135) and opens the set dialog there for #/achievements/set/<id>. The guard meant to stop a stale callback, `if (!body.isConnected && body.parentNode == null) return;` (:127), can never fire: body is a child of root, so body.parentNode is root even after KOS.show has emptied #main. So the callback draws into a detached tree and then calls openSetDialog on the new page. list() measures all 254 badges and takes 0.3-8 s on the dense account, so it is easy to leave in time (a set link from the bell, search or the Governor, then Back). Repro on slot 20 (seeded): KOS.show(achievements, set/study); 50 ms later KOS.show(home) -> 0.9 s later the Into the green set dialog is open over Home (URL #/home); after the earlier render-timing pass three such dialogs were stacked (role=dialog count 3).
findings.evidence: shots/architecture-perf/ach-set-dialog-over-home.png; eval on slot 20: {view:home, hash:#/home, dialog:CS, Maths and IT Study ... Into the green, after:911}; js/modules/achievements.js:126-135
findings.fix: Make the guard `if (!body.isConnected) return;` (or compare a render token / KOS.currentNav() with the one at call time), and the same in governor-ui.js:358/527/732, whose callbacks have no guard at all. Long term: the view lifecycle (AbortController per view) recommended in the backlog.
findings.rootCause: A wrong staleness check (parentNode of an inner node is never null) on an async render callback; no shared per-view cancellation token.

findings.title: Every boot runs the exam cap pass over all cards (0.7-1 s) and readiness about fifteen times before the first page settles
findings.detail: main.js:138 calls KOS.srs.examPass() synchronously on every boot. It walks every scheduled card and, for each, examFor() searches every capped exam with e.leaves.indexOf(sid:ref) — a linear scan of an array of leaf keys (js/core/srs.js:182-191, 201-222), so the cost is cards x exams x leaves, and recordMemory/weights() is recomputed per card. On the dense account (5,442 cards, 11 upcoming assessments) one pass takes 0.7-1.0 s and moves nothing (returns 0) — it is only useful the first boot after an exam is added. In the same boot KOS.exams.readiness ran 15 times (1.8 s, 0.7 s and a dozen of 50-100 ms; Home focus plan, notices, the badge sweep and predictedAtExam each re-derive it), and today.build 2.8 s. Measured with a boot wrapper (arch20/bootsteps.mjs; machine at load 6-7, so absolute figures are inflated about 2-3x, the ratios hold).
findings.evidence: node arch20/bootsteps.mjs 20 → [show 13708 ms (the restored Wall), today.build 2830, srs.examPass 2772, exams.readiness 1826, 658, 97, 86 ... x15, exams.freezePass 203]; eval: examPass 1010 ms then 712 ms, returns 0; readiness over 11 upcoming exams 1300 ms; js/main.js:138; js/core/srs.js:182-222
findings.fix: Build a Set of leaf keys per exam once in examIndex (or a leaf->exam map) so examFor is O(1); hoist weights(); run examPass only when its inputs changed (a hash of the cap list and the exam-day target kept in state.srsCfg) or in an idle callback after first paint. Memoise readiness per assessment on a store revision (the memo layer in the backlog).
findings.rootCause: Pure derive-on-read functions with linear lookups, called from several boot paths without a memo or a changed-inputs check.

findings.title: ~110 lines of dead CSS: the retired Habits page (79 lines of .k-hb-*) and canvas-era lab classes
findings.detail: Of 5,312 .k- class names defined in css/, 66 appear nowhere in js/ or index.html and are not built from a prefix. 33 are the old Habits page in css/views/productivity.css (79 lines matching k-hb-, from line 378) which Routines replaced in kos-routines-1 (js/modules/routines.js:491 aliases #/tasks to Routines; no JS writes k-hb-). 23 are lab classes in css/views/labs.css (k-lab-rec-*, k-lab-bitmap-*, k-lab-fsm-*, k-lab-subnet-*, k-lab-reg-*...) left from the labs before every sim moved to the SVG stage. findings.title: The 112-suite smoke gate takes ~14 CPU-minutes with no runner, no npm script and no CI; two suites are 41% of it
findings.detail: Running every suite (4 in parallel) in this tree: all 112 pass, summed runtime 849 s; smoke75 (Code content gate) 189 s and smoke56 (render purity) 163 s are 41%; next smoke44 25 s, smoke76 20 s, smoke45 20 s. The documented way to run it is a shell for-loop in CLAUDE.md; package.json has no scripts (not even 'test'), jsdom/fake-indexeddb are the only deps, there is no .github/workflows, so the gate runs only when an agent remembers to run it, sequentially (~14 min). The suites total 38,936 lines; 78 of 112 read source files with readFileSync (source-text assertions, e.g. smoke55's CSS vocabulary), which is useful for invariants but brittle to refactors such as the hub.js split.
findings.evidence: arch20/gate-summary.txt; cat package.json; ls .github -> none | earlier: /tmp timing run: count 111 + smoke.test.js run separately (3 s), sum 849 s, no failures; package.json (no scripts); ls .github/workflows -> none; wc -l tools/smoke*.test.js = 38936
findings.fix: Add tools/run_smoke.mjs that runs suites in parallel (os.cpus()-1) with a summary and non-zero exit, and 'npm test' pointing to it; a GitHub Actions workflow on push to main for the fast suites (skip the .NET/SQLite differentials). Split smoke75 so the content check runs only when js/data/content/code-* changed.
findings.rootCause: Suites were added one per release without a harness.
findings.recheck: changed: now 113 suites, 39,291 lines of tests, 1,227 CPU-seconds (was 849 s); smoke56 242 s and smoke75 236 s are 39%; still no npm script (package.json has only dependencies) and no .github/workflows.

findings.title: Date and formatting helpers are re-implemented per file (pad x18, addDays x14, iso/isoOf x16, hm x11, rid x8)
findings.detail: Counting 'function <name>(' across js/core, js/modules, js/labs and js/engines: pad 18 files, addDays 14, iso 10 + isoOf 6, hm 11, rid 8, clamp 5. The copies are textually different (pad()+getMonth, ('0'+x).slice(-2), String().padStart, one Date.UTC variant), several just forward to KOS.srs.addDays, and the 'today' helpers differ (iso(new Date()), KOS.srs.todayISO(), G.todayISO()). They agree today, but this is where a routine-day vs calendar-day (invariant 148) or a local vs UTC slip would hide, and each new module copies one more.
findings.evidence: grep -l per helper over js/{core,modules,labs,engines}/*.js (6 Nov) | earlier: grep -l 'function pad(' etc. over js/{core,modules,labs,engines}/*.js; grep -h -A3 'function iso(|function isoOf(' shows 5 distinct implementations
findings.fix: Add KOS.date (iso, parse, addDays, daysBetween, weekStart, hm, pad) in js/core next to srs, make KOS.srs's date functions delegate to it, and replace local copies opportunistically when a file is touched; a smoke rule can refuse new local 'function addDays(' definitions.
findings.rootCause: IIFE-per-file modules with no shared utility module for dates; copying a helper was the path of least resistance.
findings.recheck: changed: pad now in 19 files, addDays 15, iso 11 + isoOf 7, hm 11, rid 8 (the new achievements/art code added more copies).

findings.title: The smoke gate is not reliable under load: five suites fail when run three at a time and pass alone
findings.detail: Running all 113 suites with three in parallel on the shared test machine (load ~10) failed smoke2, smoke4 (vault cards not rendered in jsdom), smoke16 (wishlist cover), smoke17 (applyCosmetics not called after a pull) and smoke45 (toast announcements). Each passed when re-run alone (2-16 s). The failures are timing assumptions (fixed waits in the tests) rather than product bugs, but they make a parallel runner — the obvious answer to the gate's 20-minute CPU cost — unusable, and they would read as regressions on a slow CI machine. The gate itself is now 1,227 CPU-seconds (450 s wall with three workers); smoke56 (242 s) and smoke75 (236 s) are 39% of it.
findings.evidence: arch20/gate-summary.txt (exit code, ms, suite; sorted by time); scratchpad logs: smoke4 'STEP anime vault renders + lazy fallback…: Error: no cards rendered' tools/smoke4.test.js:390; smoke17 'applyCosmetics was not called after a remote state applied'; smoke16 TypeError tools/smoke16.test.js:550; serial re-runs all exit 0
findings.fix: Replace fixed sleeps in those five suites with waits on a condition (poll for the cards, the announcement, the applyCosmetics call); then add a parallel runner (npm test) with a per-suite timeout.
findings.rootCause: Tests wait fixed times for async work (IndexedDB, timers) inside jsdom.

findings.title: Writing, Files, Kurenai and Reports badges never hear their owners: they wait for the 30-minute sweep
findings.detail: Invariant 163 says owner events re-measure the badges that read that domain (touch, 400 ms). Eight badges own only domains that nobody touches: Handwritten, Write it out, Clipper (ink), Library (files), Conversations, On a schedule (assistant) and Week by week (reports); Marked shares ink with exams. The domains ever passed to KOS.achievements.touch are collection, creatives, exams, goals, governor, ja, mind, money, organise and study, plus the ledger types mapped in TYPE_DOMAINS (js/core/achievements.js:458-460); no call site in js/core/ink.js, files.js, the Assistant or reportstore touches ink, files, assistant or reports. So writing the tenth notebook page or saving the 25th file earns the tier up to 30 minutes later (the setInterval sweep, achievements.js:543), the unlock overlay arriving out of context. The registry has no check that every owner name is one some module touches, so a typo in an owner list fails silently the same way.
findings.evidence: grep -rhoE achievements.touch domains (collection 2, creatives 3, exams 3, goals 1, governor 1, ja 2, mind 3, money 1, organise 2, study 1); owners in js/core/achcatalogue.js:520-549 (ink, files, assistant, reports); js/core/achievements.js:446-466, 543
findings.fix: Touch ink on KOS.ink.savePage (the kos-ink event already exists), files on KOS.files.add/link, assistant on the tally write, reports on reportStore save; add a smoke113 assertion that every owner domain named in the catalogue is in a known DOMAINS list that call sites use.
findings.rootCause: Owner domains are free strings with no registry; touch call sites were added only for the domains that existed in the first owner set.

findings.title: CLAUDE.md is 186 KB (2,415 lines) loaded into every agent session, and its 271-line Current baseline is a release diary with stale entries
findings.detail: The canonical engineering reference opens by saying implementation history belongs in Git, then spends lines 9-279 on a chronological diary of some forty releases (each with its immutable URL), plus Branches (:195, last updated for 26 October), In flight: Japanese on feat/japanese (:203) and Planned 22 October: the iPad and Creatives (:266) - both long released. The Navigation hierarchy still lists Productivity: Focus, Reminders, Habits, Calendar (:2370) and invariant 50b names Habits (:836) although Habits became Routines (invariant 142). At ~47k tokens it is loaded whole into every coding-agent session (and AGENTS.md, README and PROGRESS repeat parts of it with different numbers - see the docs-drift finding), so stale lines are actively read as instructions. The invariants (1,800 lines) are the valuable part and are mostly accurate.
findings.evidence: wc -c CLAUDE.md = 186,526; awk: Current baseline = 271 lines; CLAUDE.md:195, 203, 266, 836, 2370
findings.fix: Cut Current baseline to five lines (production URL, current sw version, smoke gate, migrations applied, where the roadmap is) and move the release diary to docs/RELEASES.md or Git tags; fix Habits -> Routines; consider splitting the invariants per domain into docs/invariants/<domain>.md with CLAUDE.md keeping the index and the cross-cutting ones.
findings.rootCause: Each release appended a paragraph to the baseline instead of replacing it.
